item.title: SAFETY & SECURITY OFFICER _ BORNO STATE
item.description:
Country: Nigeria
Organization: INTERSOS
Closing date: 31 Dec 2099

JOB PURPOSE

Under the supervision of the Security Manager Support the risk management, in all locations. Ensure an adequate level of situational awareness to support and perform risk analysis of the local security situation. Analyze main security threat at field level and provide advice. Ensure that Safety and Security equipment are available and ensure support in establishment of risk treatment measure and access issues are followed up.

Support in ensuring that structures and systems for safety and security management are in place and respected.

.

RESPONSIBILITIES/ TASKS

  • In close cooperation with the Field Coordinator, conduct security risk assessments in new areas/routes, and advise them on security measures to be implemented.
  • Establish and maintain an active information network with other NGOs, UN, formal and informal community leaders, and national and international security actors operating in the area to obtain credible and relevant safety information.
  • Coordinate and liaise with police, security forces and relevant authorities to effectively communicate INTERSOS operations and modus operandi in order to build reliable levels of acceptance and enhance accessibility to the areas of operations.
  • Support the Field Coordinator in the establishment of security plans and procedures in the areas of operations, providing inputs on existing documents, updating information on tools and identifying procedures to revise and suggest new ones. Support Field Coordinator and the Security manager in decision making and coordination with other third parties when needed.
  • Support the sharing of information about the security tools in place and different measures in coordination with the Field Coordinator. In coordination with the Field Coordinator Conduct induction sessions to field staffs whenever necessary.
  • Provide Safety, Security and Risk Management training when needed. If not possible in person identify possible providers or remote-on-line solution.
  • Report to the line manager the progress of on-going procedures and alert in case of change of legislation in government procedures if impacting on the safety and security of the operations.
  • Identify the applied safety and security need and coordinate with logistic for their establishment.
  • Daily check on security and safety road conditions and inform the Field Coordinator. If needed also the Security Coordinator.
  • Track the staff’s movements
  • Regularly collect data on security incidents. Provide assistance in the management and follow up of incidents affecting INTERSOS project staffs and offices, sharing reliable reporting with the line manager
  • Conduct basic training to drivers, guards and staffs on topics identified by the line manager (alert system, tracking, access control, etc.)
  • Guarantee the proper set up of safety equipment and measures in place in vehicles and premises. Contribute to the proper set up and monitoring of the safe rooms
  • Represent INTERSOS at security meetings or fora, and in meetings with communities and government and non-government stakeholders and administrative and security services to obtain documents and relevant information and to negotiate access to the field, and prepare regular reports
  • Perform other security-related tasks assigned by the Security Manager

Education

  • University Degree in relevant field (Social Sciences, Psychology, Social Work, Human Rights, International Humanitarian Law or other fields related to social development and humanitarian work)
  • Master’s degree in human Rights, International Humanitarian Law or other fields related desirable
  • .

Experience

Professional experience

  • Minimum 3 years of working experience as Security Officer in a humanitarian/recovery context or relevant working experience in safety, security and risk analysis

Professional requirements

  • Good understanding of humanitarian safety practices, procedures and principles and their application
  • Experience, based on evidence, of humanitarian negotiation (with national authorities, local authorities, non-state actors, military forces) and humanitarian access in complex emergencies
  • Experience in reporting and emergency response planning

Personal requirements

  • Moral integrity
  • Teamwork and communication skills
  • Networking skills
    .

Languages

  • Proficiency in English (written and spoken)
  • Knowledge and fluency in English and local languages (Hausa and Kanuri) will be an asset.

How to apply

Interested candidates should complete this Form and attach their CV with Cover Letter following this format

“Surname_ Position you applied for”.

Application Deadline: apply not later than Monday, 30th November 2026 by 12:00 PM.

ONLY applicants whose competencies meet the requirements of the position will be contacted.

Please note: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. INTERSOS reserves the right to close the advertisement before the stated closing date if a suitable candidate is identified.

INTERSOS is committed to achieving workforce diversity in terms of gender, nationality, and culture. Individuals from minority groups, indigenous groups, Women and persons with disabilities are equally encouraged to apply.

item.title: Communications Adviser
item.description:
Country: Solomon Islands
Organization: DT Global
Closing date: 31 Dec 2099

Program Background

Pacific Australia Skills is a significant Australian investment which stands to make a major contribution to supporting social and economic growth in the region through strengthening the skills and training sector across the Pacific and Timor-Leste. Pacific Australia Skills builds on the achievements of 17 years of Australian Government support for skills and training in the Pacific.

About DT Global Asia Pacific

At DT Global Asia Pacific, we aim to positively impact people’s lives through delivery excellence. As a leading implementing partner across Asia and the Pacific, we co-create locally led solutions in partnership with governments, communities, and stakeholders. We bring together talented teams and deep regional expertise to deliver initiatives that promote inclusive economic growth, essential services, and resilient, secure communities. With over 1,500 staff, experts in 22+ countries and more than 60 years of development experience, we tackle complex community, national and transnational challenges — from governance and justice systems to climate resilience, infrastructure and social equity — with innovative thinking and a commitment to long-term impact.

For more information, please see www.dt-global.com

The Role

The Communications Adviser will provide critical strategic communications support to the Pacific Australia Skills Solomon Islands Country Office, including the SIRIS program. This role will serve as key country-level communications support for Pacific Australia Skills in Solomon Islands, integrating activity planning, preparation, and implementation with the program-wide Pacific Australia Skills Communications Strategy and the Australian High Commission’s public diplomacy strategy. In this role, the Communications Adviser will be responsible for managing the Solomon Islands Communications Coordinator and liaising closely with the Pacific Australia Skills Regional Communications Team and Australian High Commission.

Roles and Responsibilities

Strategic communications

  • Develop, implement and regularly review the SIRIS communications strategy, ensuring alignment with the program-wide Pacific Australia Skills Communications Strategy, program goals, DFAT requirements and stakeholder priorities.
  • Provide strategic communications advice to program leadership, partners and stakeholders on reputation management, messaging, stakeholder engagement and communications risks.
  • Identify opportunities to enhance program visibility, promote achievements and strengthen the profile of the Australian High Commission, Pacific Australia Skills, SIRIS and program partners.

Communications capability development and mentoring

  • Provide leadership, supervision and mentoring to communications personnel and relevant program staff.
  • Foster a culture of collaboration, accountability, continuous improvement and high performance.
  • Support communications capability strengthening initiatives with program partners and stakeholders.
  • Actively contribute to the fortnightly Pacific Australia Skills Communications Community of Practice.

Stakeholder engagement and relationship management

  • Establish and maintain effective working relationships with government representatives, national regulatory authorities, development partners, donors, civil society organisations, implementing partners and other key stakeholders.
  • Support stakeholder engagement activities and ensure communications initiatives contribute to productive partnerships and collaborative outcomes.
  • Liaise with donor representatives and partner organisations to ensure communications activities are coordinated, timely and responsive to stakeholder needs.
  • Support the development of Pacific Australia Skills and SIRIS communications materials for technical meetings, working groups and sector consultations as required.

Communications products and content development

  • Lead the development, review and quality assurance of a wide range of communications materials, including media releases, speeches, talking points, briefing notes, newsletters, social media content, reports, case studies, success stories and other promotional materials.
  • Ensure all communication products are clear, accurate, evidence-based and tailored to relevant audiences.
  • Maintain high editorial standards and ensure communications outputs comply with branding, accessibility and DFAT requirements.
  • Coordinate with the Regional Communications Team for messaging, graphic design, branding and approvals.

Event management

  • Lead the planning, coordination and delivery of program events, including high-level meetings, workshops, skills competitions, conferences and stakeholder engagement activities.
  • Ensure event planning and implementation appropriately considers protocol requirements, stakeholder expectations and donor visibility requirements.
  • Oversee event communications, promotional activities and post-event reporting.

Program management and coordination

  • Manage communications workplans, budgets and delivery schedules to ensure activities are completed on time and to a high standard.
  • Coordinate communications activities across program teams and workstreams, ensuring consistency of messaging and approach.
  • Monitor and report on communications activities, outcomes and performance, and identify opportunities for improvement.
  • Other tasks and duties, as required, to ensure the smooth and effective delivery of Pacific Australia Skills.
  • This ToR may vary and change in future.

Selection Criteria

Essential Experience and Knowledge

  • At least five years of experience in communications roles, working on DFAT-funded projects is a strong advantage. Experience working in Solomon Islands and the wider Pacific region is also highly regarded.
  • Demonstrated experience developing and implementing communications strategies that support program objectives, strengthen stakeholder engagement, and enhance organisational visibility and reputation.
  • Proven experience planning and delivering complex events, including high-level meetings, conferences, and others which involve attention to governmental protocol requirements.
  • Demonstrated ability to establish and maintain productive relationships and work collaboratively with clients, donors, government representatives, development partners, civil society organisations and others.
  • Proven ability to lead, supervise, mentor, and develop communications staff or multidisciplinary teams, fostering high performance, accountability, collaboration, and continuous improvement. Experience engaging with partners and stakeholders for communications capability development is also highly regarded.
  • Strong ability to research, synthesize, and edit a broad range of communications products including media releases, talking points, social media content, success stories and others.
  • Exceptional attention to detail and ability to ensure high-quality communication products, including compliance with branding and accessibility guidelines.
  • Program management skills, including excellent time management skills, the ability to manage multiple priorities and lead high-quality delivery of outputs in a fast-paced environment.
  • Experience providing strategic communications advice to senior leaders, donors and other partners.
  • Willingness to travel throughout Solomon Islands to support program implementation and communications, including staying overnight in rural and remote locations.

Desirable

  • Experience with developing and managing the creation of visual communications, particularly the production of video content.
  • Understanding of and commitment to Gender Equality, Disability and Social Inclusion (GEDSI), Child Protection, Prevention of Sexual Exploitation, Abuse and Harassment (PSEAH), prevention of human trafficking, environmental protection, anti-corruption and other DFAT safeguarding policies.
  • DT Global strongly encourages applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds including first nations, diverse SOGIESC and people with disabilities.
  • People with lived experience of the regions in which Pacific Australia Skills operate are strongly encouraged to apply.

Click on the link or copy paste it to access the full Terms of Reference: https://tinyurl.com/3rarxabs

How to apply

Click the link to apply: .Communication Adviser

APPLICATIONS CLOSE: 11:59pm Fiji time, Sunday 13 December 2026.

Should this role be of interest, we encourage you to apply as soon as possible. All applications will be reviewed on a 'rolling basis'. Kindly note only shortlisted applicants will be contacted.

People with lived experience of the regions in which DT Global operates are strongly encouraged to apply. DT Global welcomes applications from individuals with diverse backgrounds including First Nations peoples, diverse Sexual Orientation, Gender Identity and Expression, and Sex Characteristics (SOGIESC), and people with disabilities.

We take a zero-tolerance approach to sexual exploitation, abuse and harm of adults and children; fraud, corruption and bribery; modern slavery; and any form of exploitation across our operations, partnerships, and supply chains. We uphold the highest standards of integrity and expect the same of those we work with.

Engagement with DT Global is subject to formal background screening, criminal record checks, employment verification, and periodic compliance checks. All DT Global staff receive safety, compliance, safeguarding and integrity training, and we expect our personnel and partners to always act in alignment with our company values.

item.title: Consultancy: Mid-Term Review of the BELIEVE Project.
item.description:
Country: Kenya
Organization: CBM Global Disability Inclusion
Closing date: 31 Dec 2099

Background

CBM Global Disability Inclusion is seeking a consultancy firm to undertake the mid-term review of the Bungoma Enhancing Localised, Inclusive, Efficient, Vision Engagement (BELIEVE) Project.

BELIEVE is a KES 79 million inclusive eye health project implemented in Bungoma County by InterChristian Fellowships’ Evangelical Mission (IcFEM Mission), through Dreamland Mission Hospital, in partnership with the County Government of Bungoma, Organisations of Persons with Disabilities (OPDs) and other health, rehabilitation and referral partners, supported By CBM Global Disability Inclusion. The project runs from March 2025 to December 2027.

Its interventions cover improving accessibility of eye health services, community eye screening and treatment, referral and follow-up, rehabilitation, provision of assistive devices and psychosocial support, economic empowerment for specified groups, community-led advocacy, health-system strengthening and organisational capacity development.

Project objectives

Overall objective

To contribute towards reducing the burden of preventable blindness in Kenya.

Specific objective

To strengthen access to and delivery of inclusive, comprehensive eye health services in the Western Region of Kenya.

The project pursues this objective through four interconnected result areas:

  1. Result 1: Improved access to inclusive eye health services for rural communities in Bungoma County.
  2. Result 2: Integrated health, rehabilitation and development services available to communities in Bungoma County.
  3. Result 3: Enhanced community-led advocacy for inclusive services.
  4. Result 4: IcFEM supported to deliver an inclusive and sustainable eye health project.

Purpose of the consultancy

The overall objective of the mid-term review is to assess the project’s progress and overall direction, including whether implementation remains on track towards achieving its intended results and to identify any adjustments required to strengthen implementation during the remaining project period.

The review will identify key achievements, challenges, and lessons learned and provide practical recommendations to strengthen implementation during the remaining project period.

The specific objectives of the mid-term review are to:

  1. Assess the project’s continuing relevance to the eye health, rehabilitation, disability inclusion and wider development priorities of communities in Bungoma County.
  2. Assess the effectiveness and continuity of the service pathway from community identification and screening through referral, treatment, rehabilitation, follow-up and functional outcomes.
  3. Assess the extent to which disability inclusion, gender equality, accessibility, safeguarding, reasonable accommodation and accountability to project participants have been integrated across the eye health, rehabilitation, advocacy and economic empowerment interventions.
  4. Assess progress towards sustainability, including county ownership, financing, staffing, equipment use and maintenance, referral systems, institutional capacity, and Community Health Promoters and community structures.
  5. Review the quality and use of the project’s monitoring, evaluation and learning system, including indicator definitions, data completeness, accuracy, consistency, disaggregation and use of evidence for decision-making, to strengthen IcFEM’s monitoring and evaluation capacity for the remaining period and any subsequent phase.

Key evaluation questions

The consulting firm will refine the key evaluation questions so that the mid-term review generates the information needed on the project’s progress since inception and the overall performance of its indicators. The questions must align with the project objectives and adequately cover all outcome and result indicators. The following questions are proposed, organised by objective level; the consultant may suggest changes or additional questions at the inception stage.

Overall and specific objective

  1. To what extent does the project remain relevant to the eye health, rehabilitation and disability inclusion needs of women, men, girls, boys and persons with disabilities in the project area?
  2. What progress has the project made towards strengthening access to and delivery of inclusive, comprehensive eye health services in Bungoma County, as measured by its outcome indicators?

Result 1: Access to inclusive eye health services

  1. How effective have community screening, referral and follow-up mechanisms been in increasing access to eye care services for rural communities, including persons with disabilities?
  2. Are the activities sufficient to improve the access to inclusive eye health services for rural communities in Bungoma County? What can be improved in that area within the project timeframe? What could be done differently if scaling up the initiative?

Result 2: Integrated health, rehabilitation and development services

  1. To what extent have rehabilitation, assistive devices and psychosocial support been linked with eye health services and reached the clients who need them?
  2. To what extent have project-supported households, including persons with disabilities, strengthened their capacity to adapt and sustain economic empowerment strategies over time?
  3. Is the project on track to achieve integrated health and development services in Bungoma? What can be improved in that area within the project timeframe? Are there any best practices related to that which could be replicated if scaling up the initiative?

Result 3: Community-led advocacy

  1. How well has the collaboration between OPDs and health service providers been established so far by the project, and what is its impact, if any, on improving accessibility of eye health services for persons with disabilities? What can be improved in that area within the project timeframe? Are there any best practices related to that which could be replicated if scaling up the initiative?

Result 4: IcFEM capacity

  1. To what extent has IcFEM’s capacity to deliver an inclusive and sustainable eye health project been strengthened, including its monitoring, evaluation and learning systems?

Efficiency, coherence, sustainability and learning

  1. How efficiently have project resources been used, and is the remaining budget aligned with outstanding activities and targets?
  2. How sustainable are the results achieved so far, and what progress has been made on the project’s transition and exit commitments?
  3. What factors have contributed to or constrained project performance?
  4. How coherent is the project with other eye health, disability and livelihood interventions in Bungoma County, including the County Government’s partnership with Sightsavers on subsidised spectacles and the CBM Global-funded Bungoma Inclusive Climate Resilience Project implemented by the Kenya Red Cross Society?
  5. What early signs of change, and what unintended positive or negative effects, has the project produced so far, including for persons with disabilities, women and children?

Scope of the review

The review will cover all four project result areas listed above and their respective activities.

Fieldwork will cover selected project sites across Bungoma County, including Dreamland Mission Hospital, supported facilities in Kimilili, Webuye, Mt Elgon and Cheptais, and selected Local Transformation Unit and community sites.

Participants will include service users with and without disabilities, caregivers, Community Health Promoters, community leaders, OPDs, county and sub-county health officials, facility staff, implementing-partner personnel, referral partners and CBM Global staff.

Methodology

The consulting firm is expected to propose the most appropriate study design, sampling methods, sample size, and data collection and analysis approaches for the mid-term review. These should be clearly outlined in the technical proposal. The review of the proposal will determine whether the consulting firm will qualify to the next selection stage (interview). The consultant should identify and justify the target respondents or data sources that can effectively address the log frame indicators, including referring to the baseline data and project design documents. The proposed methodology should incorporate triangulation of findings and ensure an adequate, representative sample of the target beneficiaries, with clearly defined sampling procedures and data disaggregated by sex, age and disability status.

Project log frame

The project’s overall objective, specific objective and result-level indicators are shown in the table below.

Objective level

Indicators

Overall objective

To contribute towards reducing the burden of preventable blindness in Kenya.

Prevalence of vision-impairing eye conditions

Specific objective

To strengthen access to and delivery of inclusive, comprehensive eye health services in the Western Region of Kenya.

1. Coverage of comprehensive eye health services and referrals

2. Percentage increase in eye health service access

Result 1

Improved access to inclusive eye health services for rural communities in Bungoma County.

1. Number of people screened or examined for eye diseases to prevent blindness or low vision

2. Percentage of cataract operations carried out that led to good outcomes

3. Number of vulnerable people benefiting from the subsidy package for successful eye-related surgeries

4. Number of informal or non-professional health workers (e.g., family carers, teachers, volunteers, community members) provided with health-related training

5. Number of eye-related assistive devices provided to people with visual impairment

6. Improvement in accessibility score at participating health facilities

7. Number of accessibility plans implemented

Result 2

Integrated health, rehabilitation and development services available to communities in Bungoma County.

1. Number of people accessing mental health services provided in health systems supported by CBM Global

2. Number of assistive devices (non-eye-related) provided to people with physical and hearing impairments

3. Number of people supported to start income-generating activities

4. Number of referred eye health cases successfully linked to comprehensive services

Result 3

Enhanced community-led advocacy for inclusive services.

1. Number of formal OPDs and informal representative organisations (e.g., peer groups, self-help groups, parent groups) engaging in advocacy work

2. Number of documented cases of improved health-seeking behaviour

Result 4

IcFEM supported to deliver an inclusive and sustainable eye health project.

Demonstration of improved knowledge as a result of training among project implementing staff (IcFEM and Dreamland Mission Hospital)

The full project logframe, including means of verification and annual targets, and the baseline survey report (November 2025) will be shared with the selected consulting firm at inception. Where baseline values or targets have not yet been set, the consulting firm is expected to establish mid-term values and propose realistic end-of-project targets.

Ethical standards

The consulting firm shall take all reasonable steps to ensure that the mid-term review is designed and conducted to respect and protect the rights and welfare of the people and communities involved, and that the assessment is technically accurate and reliable, is conducted in a transparent and impartial manner, and contributes to organisational learning and accountability.

In particular, the consulting firm will:

• Obtain informed consent from all participants, explaining the purpose of the review, how information will be used and their right to decline or withdraw at any time without any effect on the services they receive.

• Provide information and consent in accessible formats, such as easy-read, Kiswahili and local languages, audio, braille or large print, and sign language interpretation, and provide reasonable accommodation so that persons with disabilities can take part on an equal basis.

• Obtain consent from a parent or guardian, and the agreement of the child, before involving any participant under 18 years of age, and interview children only in safe and visible settings.

• Keep personal data confidential, store it securely, limit access to authorised team members and anonymise data in all reports and datasets.

• Ensure that no participant is excluded or disadvantaged based on disability, sex, age or any other status.

• Remain independent and objective, declare any conflict of interest, and report findings accurately and transparently.

• Obtain any ethical or administrative approvals required by the County Government of Bungoma before data collection begins.

• Report any safeguarding concern, including sexual exploitation, abuse or harassment, immediately through CBM Global’s reporting channels.

Compliance with CBM Global policies

The selected consultancy firm will be required to sign and comply with the CBM Global Code of Conduct, Safeguarding Policy and Behaviour Code, and Accessibility Policy. The applicable policies and documents will be provided upon contracting.

Canvassing of any kind, whether direct or indirect and intended to influence the selection process, will result in immediate disqualification from consideration.

Key deliverables

• Inception report, including the evaluation matrix, methodology, sampling framework, tools and detailed work plan.

• Fieldwork debriefs presentation.

• Stakeholder validation and action-planning workshop.

• Draft mid-term review report.

• Final report of no more than 30 pages, excluding annexes, with a response-to-comments log.

• Accessible easy-read summary and stakeholder presentation.

• Clean, anonymised quantitative and qualitative datasets and data-collection tools.

Duration of the assignment

The assignment is expected to take up to 28 working days, with final deliverables due by 22 January 2027. The consulting firm is responsible for proposing, in the technical proposal, a detailed work plan showing how the assignment will be completed within the 28 days. Because fieldwork will fall over the December and January holiday period, the work plan should show how data collection will be scheduled around public holidays and the availability of county officials and other key informants.

Required qualifications and experience

• A master’s degree or higher in public health, ophthalmology or eye health management, disability studies, development studies, monitoring and evaluation, or a related field.

• At least seven years of experience designing and leading evaluations or reviews of health or development programmes, including at least three mid-term or final evaluations that can be cited and reports shared for cross-checking.

• Demonstrated experience in eye health, health-systems strengthening or rehabilitation programmes in Kenya or East Africa.

• Strong competency in participatory and mixed-methods research, quantitative and qualitative analysis, and basic financial and value-for-money analysis, as well as inclusive methodologies.

• Knowledge of Kenya’s devolved health system, county planning and budgeting processes, and the Social Health Authority.

• Strong safeguarding experience and practice.

• Excellent written and spoken English and fluency in Kiswahili. Knowledge of languages spoken in Bungoma County is an added advantage.

Applications from teams that reflect diversity and inclusion, including persons with disabilities and equitable gender representation, particularly those based in Western Kenya, are strongly encouraged.

Application requirements

• A technical proposal of no more than 7 pages, covering understanding of the assignment, proposed methodology and sampling, accessibility and safeguarding approach, work plan and team composition.

• A detailed financial proposal in Kenya shillings, including daily rates, travel, data collection, translation and other costs, inclusive of all applicable taxes (VAT and withholding tax). The financial proposal must be submitted as a separate file from the technical proposal, and no more than 3 pages.

• Summary CVs of all proposed team members, limited to three pages per person.

• A recent evaluation report prepared by the lead consultant, preferably in health or disability inclusion.

• Contact details for three referees from similar recent assignments.

• Registration documents and a valid Kenya Revenue Authority tax compliance certificate, where applicable.

Selection criteria

Bids that are incomplete or missing mandatory documents, including registration documents and a valid KRA tax compliance certificate, will not be evaluated further.

The final score will combine the technical score (70%) and the financial score (30%).

Payment schedule

Payments will be made against approved invoices and in accordance with CBM Global’s consultancy invoicing requirements. The consultancy fee and any reimbursable costs will be agreed during contracting. Payments will be made as follows:

• 50% upon acceptance of the inception package.

• 50% upon delivery and approval of the final report and all remaining deliverables.

How to apply

Application documents as listed under “Application requirements” above, with the technical and financial proposals as separate files, should be sent by email to CBM Global at procurement.kenya@cbm-global.org with the subject “BELIEVE Mid-Term Review” by 1700 hours East Africa Time on 4 December 2026. Any proposals received after the stated time and date will be automatically rejected.

Proposals that do not follow the guidelines above will be rejected.

Any queries should be sent to: Kevin.Sudi@cbm-global.org, with procurement.kenya@cbm-global.org in copy (CC) by 30th November 2026.

Only shortlisted applicants will be contacted. CBM Global is committed to equal opportunities. Applicants with disabilities are encouraged to apply, and reasonable accommodation will be provided during the selection process upon request.

item.title: Independent Gender, Protection, and Inclusion Specialist Consultancy Services
item.description:
Organization: Center for Operational Analysis and Research
Closing date: 31 Dec 2099

Scope of Services

Nature of Services: Independent Gender, Protection, and Inclusion Specialist Consultancy Services

Type of Contract: Services will be provided on a day-rate basis against specific project assignments, with the applicable scope, deliverables, estimated level of effort, and fees agreed in writing between COAR and the Consultant.

Level of Effort: Assignment-based and strictly as mutually agreed in writing for specific tasks and deliverables. No minimum number of days, fixed working hours, or continuing level of effort is guaranteed or required.

Place of Performance: Such location as determined by the Consultant when performing the Services subject to any location-specific requirements expressly agreed in writing for a particular assignment. Any travel, in-person attendance, location-specific requirements and associated expenses shall be agreed in advance.

Overview: This Scope of Services (SoS) outlines the services that may be provided by an Independent Gender, Protection, and Inclusion Specialist Consultant to the Center for Operational Analysis and Research (COAR). The Consultant shall provide technical expertise to ensure the systematic integration of gender equality, disability inclusion, protection, and Leave No One Behind (LNOB) principles throughout the evaluation of the Joint Programme. The Consultant shall assess the extent to which programme interventions have promoted equitable participation, strengthened social cohesion, addressed the needs of vulnerable population groups, and ensured inclusive access to services, resources, and opportunities.

Nature of the consultancy: This is an independent, non-exclusive, project-based consultancy engagement and not a position of employment with COAR. Services will be commissioned through specific assignments agreed between COAR and the Consultant, setting out the relevant scope, deliverables, estimated level of effort, timeframe and applicable day rate.

COAR does not guarantee any minimum number of assignments or consultancy days, and the Consultant will remain free to accept or decline proposed assignments and to provide services to other clients, subject to confidentiality, conflicts of interest and the timely delivery of any assignment accepted.

The Consultant will determine independently the professional approach, methods, sequencing, working time and place of performance of the Services, subject to agreed deliverables, deadlines, applicable legal, contractual, client, security, safeguarding, confidentiality, data-protection, and other project-specific requirements, and reasonable project coordination. The Consultant will ordinarily use their own equipment and working facilities and will be responsible for their own tax, social insurance and other statutory obligations arising from the consultancy. The consultancy does not carry employee benefits.

The Consultant will coordinate their own activities and agreed project inputs but will not occupy a position within COAR’s organisational structure, exercise employment or line-management authority over COAR personnel, or have authority to bind COAR, except where expressly authorised in writing for a defined project purpose.

COAR may specify the scope, required outputs, deadlines, quality standards, project requirements, and information required for an agreed assignment, but will not direct the Consultant as to the manner or means of performing the Services.

The Consultant will not be required to work fixed hours, maintain continuous availability, attend COAR premises on a regular basis, or participate in COAR’s internal management or personnel processes, except where specific attendance or participation is reasonably necessary for an agreed assignment.

Fees will be payable only for Services performed under an agreed assignment and against submission of appropriate invoices. No minimum volume of work or continuing retainer is guaranteed.

Activities

The activities may include, as agreed between the parties, but not be limited to:

  • Gender Equality and Women's Empowerment Assessment: Examine the extent to which programme interventions have addressed gender inequalities, promoted women's participation and empowerment, and contributed to equitable access to services, resources, and economic opportunities.
  • Disability Inclusion and LNOB Assessment: Assess the accessibility, inclusiveness, and responsiveness of programme interventions to the needs and priorities of persons with disabilities and other marginalised or vulnerable population groups.
  • Protection and Safeguarding Analysis: Evaluate the integration and effectiveness of protection, safeguarding, accountability, and do-no-harm considerations across programme design, implementation, and service delivery.
  • Social Cohesion and Community Participation: Assess programme contributions to inclusive community engagement, participation in decision-making, social cohesion, and conflict-sensitive approaches, including the representation of diverse population groups.
  • Inclusive Evaluation Methodology: Provide technical guidance on the design and implementation of inclusive and gender-sensitive evaluation methodologies, ensuring appropriate participation and representation across different population groups and the application of ethical and safeguarding standards in data collection.
  • Differential Outcomes Analysis: Examine how programme benefits, outcomes, and impacts have varied across population groups, including by gender, age, disability, displacement status, and other relevant vulnerability factors.
  • Cross-Cutting Integration and Recommendations: Ensure gender equality, disability inclusion, protection, social cohesion, and LNOB considerations are systematically reflected in the evaluation's findings, conclusions, and recommendations.

Required Experience and Expertise

  • Advanced university degree (Master's level or equivalent) in Gender Studies, Social Sciences, Human Rights, Development Studies, Social Work, International Development, Disability Studies, or a related discipline.
  • At least 7–10 years of demonstrated professional experience in gender equality, social inclusion, protection, disability inclusion, or related areas, preferably within international development, humanitarian, recovery, or stabilisation programmes.
  • Proven experience assessing gender-responsive programming, women's participation and empowerment, gender-related barriers, and equitable access to services, resources, and economic opportunities.
  • Demonstrated technical knowledge of disability-inclusive programming, accessibility standards, social inclusion, and approaches to identifying and addressing the needs of marginalised and vulnerable population groups.
  • Experience assessing protection mainstreaming, safeguarding frameworks, accountability mechanisms, conflict sensitivity, and the application of do-no-harm principles in programme implementation and evaluation.
  • Proven experience assessing community participation, social cohesion, inclusive decision-making, and the engagement of diverse population groups in recovery and development interventions.
  • Demonstrated experience designing and implementing gender-sensitive, inclusive, and participatory evaluation methodologies, including qualitative research, focus group discussions, key informant interviews, and other participatory data collection approaches.
  • Strong capacity to analyse differentiated programme outcomes across population groups, applying an intersectional lens that considers gender, age, disability, displacement, socioeconomic status, and other relevant vulnerability factors.
  • Experience applying ethical research standards, informed consent, confidentiality, safeguarding protocols, and safe and accessible approaches to engaging vulnerable populations.
  • Excellent analytical, communication, and report-writing skills, with the ability to integrate cross-cutting findings into evaluation conclusions and formulate practical, evidence-based recommendations.
